title: Latent operations, and why multiplying changes the picture

questions.q: What does LatentMultiply do to an EmptyLatentImage?
options: Nothing, because it is all zeros
questions.answer: Nothing, because it is all zeros
questions.why: Zero times anything is zero, and the noise is added later in the sampler.

questions.q: Why does multiplying near the start of a run do less damage than at the end?
options: Later steps can still pull the sample back toward the data
questions.answer: Later steps can still pull the sample back toward the data
questions.why: In the lab the spread ends near 1.22 from an early multiply and 1.47 from a late one.

questions.q: A plain average of two noises has spread about:
questions.why: Independent noises add as squares: √(¼ + ¼) ≈ 0.71, measured as 0.708.
